How Many Thoughts Can a Vector Hold?
The Capacity of Reasoning by Superposition

Hongyu Gu
University of Science and Technology of China Hefei, China ustc_23ghy@mail.ustc.edu.cn    Chang Liu
Zhongguancun Academy and Technology of China Beijing, China liuchang@bza.edu.cn    Jingwen Fu
Zhongguancun Academy and Technology of China Beijing, China jwfu99@gmail.com ††thanks: Corresponding author.
Abstract

Large language models solve difficult problems by carrying intermediate computation across many reasoning steps. Conventional chain-of-thought writes this computation as tokens; recent continuous and recurrent approaches instead move part of it into fixed-dimensional latent states, where one thought can superpose several alternatives. This shift raises a basic design question: as reasoning proceeds, what should a continuous thought preserve? The natural strategy is to discard earlier computation and keep only the current frontier: storing more objects appears to dilute the state and waste its limited capacity. We show that this intuition can be exactly backwards. When the same downstream computation is applied to both states, a cumulative superposition that retains the reached history can require less representation dimension than a frontier superposition that stores only the current alternatives. At a fixed hidden width, this advantage lets a latent reasoner retain more usable evidence, distinguish more possible downstream outcomes, and delay the point at which its compressed state becomes unreliable. The reversal occurs because useful historical components reinforce one another coherently, while unrelated alternatives remain random interference. This perspective also resolves a practical design question: how should a model weight the memories accumulated inside a latent state when their future use is not yet known? Across the full family of reusable weighted superpositions, concentrating on a few recent or salient objects creates a weakly represented memory that bottlenecks later attention. Uniform cumulative weighting avoids this failure, and we prove that it is minimax-optimal for robust future reasoning. Our results turn superposition from an observed latent phenomenon into a design principle: balanced cumulative memory can make a fixed representational budget support more reliable and reusable computation.

1 Introduction

What should a continuous thought preserve as reasoning unfolds? This question is becoming increasingly relevant as language-model reasoning moves from explicit text into continuous computation. Continuous chain-of-thought feeds hidden states directly back into the model (Hao et al., 2024); looped and recurrent Transformers repeatedly update a latent workspace (Xu and Sato, 2024; Fu et al., 2026); and reasoning by superposition shows that one continuous thought can encode several search alternatives and expand them in parallel (Zhu et al., 2025b). These results establish that superposed latent reasoning is possible. They leave open a consequential question for model design: among the many superpositions that can represent a computation, which one uses a limited hidden dimension most effectively?

We study three structures that isolate this choice. A frontier superposition stores the alternatives active at the current step, a cumulative superposition stores the full reached history, and a general weighted superposition distributes representational energy arbitrarily across that history. All three use the same graph, downstream query, candidate bank, and decoder. The comparison therefore changes only what the continuous thought preserves, not the task it is asked to solve.

Ordinary capacity intuition favors frontier superposition: storing more objects in one normalized vector dilutes their individual coefficients and should make them harder to recover (Elhage et al., 2022). We show that this intuition can be exactly backwards for reasoning. Cumulative superposition can remain usable at a smaller hidden dimension despite storing strictly more objects, because useful historical components reinforce one another coherently while unrelated alternatives remain random interference. Superposition capacity is therefore governed not by support size alone, but by how the stored information supports future computation.

This reversal holds for a broad, state-independent class of downstream queries, which may be continuous, correlated, asymmetric, and identity-dependent. The condition captures bounded-influence computations over accumulated objects, including whole-set aggregation, additive route objectives, algorithmic execution traces, and intermediate-step evaluation (Zaheer et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2019; Kool et al., 2019; Veličković et al., 2022; Lightman et al., 2024).

The comparison also has a direct interpretation inside a Transformer: attention expands the current computation, while residual writing determines whether earlier objects are discarded or preserved. For general weighted superpositions, concentrating weight on a few objects leaves other memories too weak for later attention to reuse. When their future use is unknown, uniform cumulative weighting solves the resulting robust design problem:

𝒂cum∈arg⁡min𝒂⁡𝔇⁡(𝒂,𝒰C),\boldsymbol{a}_{\mathrm{cum}}\in\arg\min_{\boldsymbol{a}}\mathfrak{D}(\boldsymbol{a};\mathcal{U}_{C}), (1)

where 𝔇\mathfrak{D} is the worst-case end-to-end critical dimension. This suggests a simple principle for latent reasoning: expand the current computation while preserving its history with balanced representational weight.

Contributions.

Our main contributions are:

  1. 1.

    Critical-dimension theory. We derive an exact finite-dimensional score law and show that cumulative superposition requires fewer dimensions than frontier superposition for a broad class of nonlocalized queries. This result shifts the relevant notion of capacity from how many objects are stored to how effectively they support future computation, explaining when retaining more history benefits a fixed-width reasoner.

  2. 2.

    End-to-end Transformer mechanism. We realize both superpositions through the same attention–residual construction and identify the weakest retained coefficient as the routing bottleneck. This connects the abstract dimension advantage to multi-step Transformer computation and provides a concrete diagnostic for failures of reusable latent memory.

  3. 3.

    A minimax design principle. Across reusable weighted superpositions, uniform cumulative weighting is sharply near-optimal for fixed nonlocalized query classes and exactly minimax when future queries are unknown. This provides a robust rule for allocating latent memory, supported by width-scaling and token-level experiments in both lightweight and GPT-2 models.

2 Related Work

Explicit and continuous reasoning.

Chain-of-thought externalizes intermediate computation as tokens (Wei et al., 2022; Merrill and Sabharwal, 2024), whereas COCONUT feeds continuous thoughts back into the model (Hao et al., 2024). Recent theory shows that continuous tokens can maintain and explore several reasoning traces in parallel (Zhu et al., 2025b; Gozeten et al., 2025); subsequent work studies how such superpositions emerge during training (Zhu et al., 2025a). Our question is different from existence or learnability: among frontier, cumulative, and weighted states, which representation requires the least embedding dimension for the same later computation?

Capacity of superposition.

Feature-superposition analyses explain how non-orthogonal features share a low-dimensional space and how interference depends on feature sparsity, importance, and polysemanticity (Elhage et al., 2022; Foote, 2024; Gupta and Kumar, 2025; Bereska et al., 2025). These analyses primarily concern recovery or interpretation of individual features. Our result isolates a reasoning-specific reversal: when later computation aggregates several stored objects, additional components can contribute coherent signal, making query-aligned margin—rather than support size—the operative capacity.

Recurrent computation and latent memory.

Universal and looped Transformers reuse computation depth while maintaining a latent workspace (Dehghani et al., 2019; Giannou et al., 2023; Xu and Sato, 2024; Fu et al., 2026), while recurrent-memory and buffer-based models carry information through dedicated latent tokens (Bulatov et al., 2022; Yang et al., 2024; Lin et al., 2026). Related work studies the difficulty of multi-hop reasoning in long contexts and without explicit intermediate steps (Li et al., 2024; Yao et al., 2025), as well as limits and representations of hidden reasoning (Brown-Cohen et al., 2026; Hu et al., 2024). Our dimension laws separate two roles of this latent budget: storing atomic states and keeping a compact state aligned with computations that must reuse them later.

We first derive the dimension law for an arbitrary weighted state. Frontier and cumulative comparisons will then follow by substitution, not by changing the readout.

Remark 4.3.

The theorem turns superposition from a representational possibility into an operational criterion: a latent state is useful only when its aligned signal clears the competition created by the candidate set. Because every state is evaluated on the same task with the same decoder, the boundary isolates the effect of representation geometry and predicts a sharp failure when width is insufficient. It therefore provides the basis for asking whether retaining more reasoning history can make a fixed-width state more useful.

Corollary 4.4 (Matching critical dimension).

Fix δ∈(0,1)\delta\in(0,1). For any sequence M→∞M\to\infty and μM∈(0,1]\mu_{M}\in(0,1], the critical dimension at which superposition reasoning succeeds with high probability is

d⋆​(a,u0,M,δ)=(2+o⁡(1))​log⁡MμM2.d_{\star}(a,u_{0};M,\delta)=(2+o(1))\frac{\log M}{\mu_{M}^{2}}. (20)

where pd,M​(μ)p_{d,M}(\mu) denotes the probability in (17). Along any sequence for which min⁡{d​μ2,log⁡N}→∞\min\{d\mu^{2},\log N\}\to\infty,

log⁡Mmax=(1+o⁡(1))​min​{d​μ22,log⁡N}.\log M_{\max}=(1+o(1))\min\left\{\frac{d\mu^{2}}{2},\log N\right\}. (22)
Remark 4.5.

The matching law makes the phase transition actionable as a model-sizing rule: it specifies the hidden width required for a target reliability and the number of competing continuations that a fixed-width state can distinguish. For a continuous-reasoning model, it separates two remedies for readout failure: increase width or improve the alignment of the latent state with its future computation. Width savings can therefore be interpreted as additional usable reasoning capacity rather than merely a change in representation geometry.

5 Why Cumulative Superposition Wins

We now answer three questions. When cumulative needs fewer dimensions? How a Transformer implements its update, and whether another weighting can do better once the full history must remain usable?

5.1 Cumulative needs fewer dimensions

Task regime.

Nonlocalization is a state-independent bounded-influence condition, it constrains only the downstream query uu and never compares its alignments with aRa_{R} and aFa_{F}. Since ‖u‖2=1\left\|u\right\|_{2}=1, a fixed CC means that every query draws on at least m/C2m/C^{2} reached objects, Such readouts arise naturally in set and multiset aggregation, additive objectives over visited objects, and supervision over algorithmic or reasoning traces (Zaheer et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2019; Kool et al., 2019; Veličković et al., 2022; Lightman et al., 2024). Continuous and superposed reasoning provide the corresponding state geometry of multi-step latent search (Hao et al., 2024; Zhu et al., 2025b). On the state side, k=o⁡(m)k=o(m) says that the states activated at the current step grow more slowly than the accumulated computation. It includes chains and fixed-width traces, where k=O⁡(1)k=O(1) and m=Θ⁡(c)m=\Theta(c) at depth cc, as well as grid-like breadth-first search in dd dimensions, where k=Θ⁡(cd−1)k=\Theta(c^{d-1}) and m=Θ⁡(cd)m=\Theta(c^{d}). Fixed CC and k=o⁡(m)k=o(m) therefore capture a broad growing-history regime in which queries reuse a constant fraction of an expanding trace while its current frontier occupies a vanishing fraction.

Theorem 5.1 (Sharp separation for nonlocalized query classes).

Fix F⊊RF\subsetneq R, with |F|=k<m=|R||F|=k<m=|R|, and use the same candidate bank for both states. Let 𝒰⊆𝒜R\mathcal{U}\subseteq\mathcal{A}_{R} be any nonempty compact CC-nonlocalized query class. Then

Γ⁡(aR,𝒰)≥1C,Γ⁡(aF,𝒰)≤C​km,\Gamma(a_{R};\mathcal{U})\geq\frac{1}{C},\qquad\Gamma(a_{F};\mathcal{U})\leq C\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}, (23)

Consequently, whenever Γ⁡(aF,𝒰)>0\Gamma(a_{F};\mathcal{U})>0,

D⋆​(aR,𝒰,M,δ)D⋆​(aF,𝒰,M,δ)≤C4​km​(1+o⁡(1)).\frac{D_{\star}(a_{R};\mathcal{U},M,\delta)}{D_{\star}(a_{F};\mathcal{U},M,\delta)}\leq C^{4}\frac{k}{m}(1+o(1)). (24)

For every fixed CC, this ratio tends to zero in the growing-history regime k=o⁡(m)k=o(m); thus cumulative needs asymptotically fewer dimensions for the same query class and error. If Γ⁡(aF,𝒰)=0\Gamma(a_{F};\mathcal{U})=0, frontier instead has infinite critical dimension above chance while cumulative remains finite.

Remark 5.2.

This theorem resolves the paper’s main paradox without selecting a special query. For the broad class of nonlocalized computations that reuse an expanding history, storing the full reached set reduces rather than consumes hidden dimension, even though the state represents more objects. A cumulative latent workspace can therefore remain reliable at widths where frontier-only compression fails. For model design, discarding earlier intermediate states is not automatically capacity-efficient when later reasoning may aggregate evidence across the trace.

The reason is coherent addition. Readout succeeds when

⟨a,u⟩​d⏟useful signal≳2​log⁡M⏟unrelated competition.\underbrace{\langle a,u\rangle\sqrt{d}}_{\text{useful signal}}\gtrsim\underbrace{\sqrt{2\log M}}_{\text{unrelated competition}}. (25)

For cumulative, ⟨aR,u⟩=‖u‖1/m\langle a_{R},u\rangle=\left\|u\right\|_{1}/\sqrt{m}: useful historical components add before normalization, while unrelated candidates remain centered fluctuations. The extra stored objects therefore strengthen a history-wide computation instead of acting as independent noise. This is the mathematical source of the apparent reversal.

5.2 Transformer realization and its dimension cost

At depth cc, let Nc=Rc+1∖RcN_{c}=R_{c+1}\setminus R_{c} be the newly reached set and rc=|Nc|r_{c}=|N_{c}|. An edge token e=(s,t)e=(s,t) stores [gs;gt][g_{s};g_{t}], and the latent token stores the current superposition. A visited-edge mask exposes the current expansion candidates; we assume one active parent per node in NcN_{c} so that active destinations are averaged uniformly.

Theorem 5.3 (Transformer realization and routing dimension).

A width-O⁡(d)O(d) construction with two attention blocks, a standard residual, and RMSNorm implements the following update with vanishing error:

qc+1=RMSNorm⁡(λc​qc+ηc​oc),oc=1rc​∑t∈Ncgt+o⁡(1).q_{c+1}=\operatorname{RMSNorm}\!\left(\lambda_{c}q_{c}+\eta_{c}o_{c}\right),\qquad o_{c}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{r_{c}}}\sum_{t\in N_{c}}g_{t}+o(1). (26)

The first attention block compares the source-membership score β⁡⟨qc,gs⟩\beta\langle q_{c},g_{s}\rangle with a threshold token and writes a gate on each edge; the second averages the destinations of the gated edges. The coefficient choices

(λc,ηc)=(0,1)and(λc,ηc)=(|Rc|,rc)(\lambda_{c},\eta_{c})=(0,1)\quad\text{and}\quad(\lambda_{c},\eta_{c})=(\sqrt{|R_{c}|},\sqrt{r_{c}}) (27)

produce frontier and cumulative, respectively, while other nonnegative coefficients produce layer-weighted recursive updates. No FFN is required.

More generally, the same membership head can route from any weighted state sequence 𝐚=(ac)c=0D\boldsymbol{a}=(a_{c})_{c=0}^{D}. If every layer contains Θ⁡(n)\Theta(n) independent inactive source keys and amin,c:=minv∈Rc⁡ac,va_{\min,c}:=\min_{v\in R_{c}}a_{c,v}, its routing critical dimension is

droute​(𝒂,δ)=Θ⁡(maxc<D⁡log⁡(D​n/δ)amin,c2),d_{\mathrm{route}}(\boldsymbol{a},\delta)=\Theta\!\left(\max_{c<D}\frac{\log(Dn/\delta)}{a_{\min,c}^{2}}\right), (28)

with infinite dimension when a required coefficient is zero. For a uniform state on ss objects this reduces to Θ⁡(s​log⁡(D​n/δ))\Theta(s\log(Dn/\delta)).

Remark 5.4.

This result closes the gap between a representation-level capacity comparison and executable continuous reasoning. Frontier, cumulative, and weighted superpositions are not merely hand-designed vectors evaluated by an external decoder: the same two-block Transformer can generate them autoregressively, and the critical-dimension law also governs whether attention can propagate them reliably. Thus, the cumulative advantage applies to an implementable latent workspace, while drouted_{\mathrm{route}} gives a concrete width requirement for preserving and reusing that workspace across reasoning depth.

5.3 Cumulative is minimax under nonlocalized future use

Consider any weighted sequence readable by the Transformer membership head, 𝒂=(ac)c=0D\boldsymbol{a}=(a_{c})_{c=0}^{D} with ac∈𝒜Rca_{c}\in\mathcal{A}_{R_{c}}. If every reached object may later be queried as an edge source, its smallest coefficient controls the worst membership margin. Theorem 5.3 and Corollary 4.4 show that its actual end-to-end critical dimension is, up to universal constants, the scale

𝔇⁡(𝒂,𝒰):=max⁡{maxc<D⁡log⁡(D​n/δ)(minv∈Rc⁡ac,v)2,2​log⁡MΓ​(aD,𝒰)2}.\mathfrak{D}(\boldsymbol{a};\mathcal{U}):=\max\left\{\max_{c<D}\frac{\log(Dn/\delta)}{(\min_{v\in R_{c}}a_{c,v})^{2}},\frac{2\log M}{\Gamma(a_{D};\mathcal{U})^{2}}\right\}. (29)

This optimizes over the full weighted family 𝒜Rc\mathcal{A}_{R_{c}}, which contains the recursive updates in Theorem 5.3 as well as their two canonical endpoints.

Theorem 5.5 (Sharp universal and robust optimality of cumulative).

Suppose every reached object must remain eligible for later source-membership attention. Let 𝒰\mathcal{U} be any nonempty compact C-query class, and let 𝐚R=(aRc)c=0D\boldsymbol{a}_{R}=(a_{R_{c}})_{c=0}^{D} be the uniform cumulative sequence. Then

𝔇⁡(𝒂R,𝒰)≤C2​infac∈𝒜Rc0≤c≤D𝔇⁡(𝒂,𝒰).\mathfrak{D}(\boldsymbol{a}_{R};\mathcal{U})\leq C^{2}\inf_{\begin{subarray}{c}a_{c}\in\mathcal{A}_{R_{c}}\\ 0\leq c\leq D\end{subarray}}\mathfrak{D}(\boldsymbol{a};\mathcal{U}). (30)

The factor C2C^{2} is sharp in the readout-dominated regime. Moreover, cumulative is exactly robust-minimax over the full nonlocalized family:

𝒂R∈arg⁡minac∈𝒜Rc0≤c≤D⁡𝔇⁡(𝒂,𝒰C​(RD)).\boldsymbol{a}_{R}\in\arg\min_{\begin{subarray}{c}a_{c}\in\mathcal{A}_{R_{c}}\\ 0\leq c\leq D\end{subarray}}\mathfrak{D}(\boldsymbol{a};\mathcal{U}_{C}(R_{D})). (31)

Thus, for fixed C=O⁡(1)C=O(1), cumulative is rate-minimax-optimal for every nonlocalized query class and exactly optimal when nonlocalization is the only prior on future use.

Remark 5.6.

This result turns cumulative from one feasible endpoint into a design rule for latent reasoning. When a model cannot know in advance which part of its trace later computation will reuse, no alternative weighting achieves a smaller worst-case end-to-end width over the full nonlocalized family; for any fixed nonlocalized class, cumulative is still within the sharp C2C^{2} factor. Uniform residual accumulation is therefore a robust default, while learned or query-matched weighting is a specialization that trades away protection against other future uses.

6 Experiment

6.1 Nonlocalized separation

We test Theorem 5.1 on a grid over m∈{64,128,256,512}m\in\{64,128,256,512\}, k/m∈{1/32,…,1/2}k/m\in\{1/32,\ldots,1/2\}, C∈{1,1.25,1.5,2}C\in\{1,1.25,1.5,2\}, and M∈{210,214}M\in\{2^{10},2^{14}\}, estimating worst-case D⋆D_{\star} by binary search on dd with 20002000 Monte Carlo trials (δ=0.1\delta=0.1). Each query is drawn independently of GG and projected onto the cap ‖u‖∞≤C/m\left\|u\right\|_{\infty}\leq C/\sqrt{m}. Dense uses random positive weights on all mm coordinates, modeling uneven aggregation over a visited set (Zaheer et al., 2017). Temporal centers an exponential bump along the trace, modeling localized process supervision over a CoT (Lightman et al., 2024). Block partitions the trace into segments with different scales, modeling staged algorithmic readouts (Veličković et al., 2022). Union mixes the three generators. The sharp witness is the theorem’s example, uniform on ⌈m/C2⌉\lceil m/C^{2}\rceil coordinates that contain FF. Zero-overlap is uniform on R∖FR\setminus F, so Γ⁡(aF,𝒰)=0\Gamma(a_{F};\mathcal{U})=0.

Protocol.

We use the ProsQA(Zhong et al., 2022) graph-memory task and hold the graph trace, candidate bank, and Gaussian codebook fixed when comparing state constructions. Queries are drawn before the Gaussian map. The controlled attention experiment uses an identity-regularized source-membership router at d=192d=192 and evaluates five independent Gaussian codebooks.

6.2 Cumulative has a lower dimension threshold use

Across the paired five-seed sweeps, cumulative crosses the same 90% held-out success threshold at substantially lower width on both architectures. Its interpolated critical dimension is 40.3±1.140.3\pm 1.1, compared with 110.6±1.6110.6\pm 1.6 for frontier, in the lightweight two-block model; with the two-layer GPT-2 backbone it is 34.4±3.834.4\pm 3.8, compared with 66.2±5.966.2\pm 5.9. The corresponding cumulative/frontier ratios are 0.365±0.0080.365\pm 0.008 and 0.521±0.0670.521\pm 0.067. Thus the separation predicted by Theorem 5.1 persists when the analytic router is replaced by a trained causal Transformer. Figure 3 shows both width sweeps and their paired critical-dimension estimates under matched evaluation protocols.

6.3 Uniform weighting prevents a token-level routing bottleneck

We next test the mechanism behind Theorem 5.3. Figure 4(a) shows the predicted two-term geometry: uniform cumulative is the joint lower-left point after normalizing routing and worst-query readout width by the uniform construction. Panels (b,c) expose what this optimum means inside the router. Uniform weights equalize the coefficient of every reusable memory token; recency and random weights produce low-coefficient tokens, and those tokens receive lower membership margins. Consequently, joint route success falls from 0.9060.906 to 0.5860.586 and 0.5370.537, while the per-inactive-key false-positive rate rises from 0.03%0.03\% to 0.57%0.57\% and 1.31%1.31\%, respectively.

7 Conclusion

We characterized frontier, cumulative, and general weighted reasoning superpositions through three linked results. First, a sharp Gaussian dimension law reduces reliable readout to state–query alignment; for any fixed nonlocalized query class, cumulative requires asymptotically fewer dimensions than frontier in the growing-history regime k=o⁡(m)k=o(m). Second, two attention blocks, a residual path, and RMSNorm realize both states as endpoints of one weighted Transformer update, attention selects newly reached objects, whereas the residual determines whether previous computation is discarded or retained. The same construction shows that the smallest reusable coefficient controls routing width. Third, optimizing routing and readout jointly over the full weighted family makes uniform cumulative superposition exactly minimax-optimal when reached history remains reusable and future use is exchangeable.

These results explain the apparent paradox that storing more objects can make reasoning easier. cumulative therefore converts reusable history into coherent signal rather than additional interference. This gives “stronger” an operational meaning—fewer dimensions for the same query class, transition, and target error—and identifies cumulative as the capacity-optimal target in this regime. The analysis isolates capacity and representability under Gaussian embeddings and an isotropic candidate bank; Appendix C extends the reduction to correlated banks with positive population margins. Extending the theory to learned anisotropic codebooks and explaining when optimization discovers the required routing and weighting remain important next steps.

Proof of Theorem 5.3.

We use the standard finite-depth convention for this construction: fix DD and δ∈(0,1)\delta\in(0,1), let n→∞n\to\infty, omit empty transitions, and start from the exact intended state q0q_{0}. ℰroute(d):=⋂c<D{minv∈Rc⟨qac,gv⟩>τc>maxs∈Ic⟨qac,gs⟩}.\mathcal{E}_{\rm route}(d):=\bigcap_{c<D}\left\{\min_{v\in R_{c}}\langle q_{a_{c}},g_{v}\rangle>\tau_{c}>\max_{s\in I_{c}}\langle q_{a_{c}},g_{s}\rangle\right\}. (52)

Proof of Theorem 5.5.

Write L:=log⁡(D​n/δ)L:=\log(Dn/\delta) and B:=2​log⁡MB:=2\log M, and interpret a zero alignment or reusable coefficient as infinite width. For every c<Dc<D and every ac∈𝒜Rca_{c}\in\mathcal{A}_{R_{c}},

with equality only at ac=aRca_{c}=a_{R_{c}}. Hence the routing part of 𝔇⁡(𝒂R,𝒰)\mathfrak{D}(\boldsymbol{a}_{R};\mathcal{U}) is no larger than that of any 𝔇⁡(𝒂,𝒰)\mathfrak{D}(\boldsymbol{a};\mathcal{U}).

BΓ​(aRD,𝒰)2≤C2​B≤C2​BΓ​(aD,𝒰)2.\frac{B}{\Gamma(a_{R_{D}};\mathcal{U})^{2}}\leq C^{2}B\leq C^{2}\frac{B}{\Gamma(a_{D};\mathcal{U})^{2}}. (64)

for every weighted sequence 𝒂\boldsymbol{a}. Taking the infimum proves (30).

The factor is sharp. Suppose s:=|RD|/C2s:=|R_{D}|/C^{2} is an integer, choose S⊆RDS\subseteq R_{D} with |S|=s|S|=s, and let u=𝟏S/su=\mathbf{1}_{S}/\sqrt{s} and 𝒰={u}\mathcal{U}=\{u\}. Γ⁡(aD,𝒰C​(RD))\displaystyle\Gamma(a_{D};\mathcal{U}_{C}(R_{D})) ≤1m!​∑P⟨aD,P​u⋆⟩=‖aD‖1​‖u⋆‖1m\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{m!}\sum_{P}\langle a_{D},Pu_{\star}\rangle=\frac{\left\|a_{D}\right\|_{1}\left\|u_{\star}\right\|_{1}}{m}
≤‖u⋆‖1m=Γ⁡(aRD,𝒰C​(RD)).\displaystyle\leq\frac{\left\|u_{\star}\right\|_{1}}{\sqrt{m}}=\Gamma(a_{R_{D}};\mathcal{U}_{C}(R_{D})). (66)

Appendix C Exact Reduction for an Arbitrary Fixed Bank

The orthogonal bank makes the main dimension law transparent. The following identity shows that the same signal-versus-competition structure persists for an arbitrary fixed correlated bank.

Theorem C.1 (Arbitrary-bank Gaussian reduction).

Fix a unit state aa and deterministic candidate directions u0,u1,…,uMu_{0},u_{1},\ldots,u_{M}, independent of GG. For each j≥1j\geq 1, let

hj:=u0−uj,γj:=⟨a,hj⟩>0,rj:=hj−γj​a∈a⟂.h_{j}:=u_{0}-u_{j},\qquad\gamma_{j}:=\langle a,h_{j}\rangle>0,\qquad r_{j}:=h_{j}-\gamma_{j}a\in a^{\perp}. (67)

Let g∼N⁡(0,In)g\sim N(0,I_{n}) and Cd∼χdC_{d}\sim\chi_{d} be independent. Then

ℙ(j^(qa)=0)=ℙ(max1≤j≤M⟨g,−rj/γj⟩<Cd).\mathbb{P}(\widehat{j}(q_{a})=0)=\mathbb{P}\left(\max_{1\leq j\leq M}\langle g,-r_{j}/\gamma_{j}\rangle<C_{d}\right). (68)
Proof.

The correct candidate beats candidate jj exactly when

0\displaystyle 0 <⟨G​a,G⁡(u0−uj)⟩\displaystyle<\langle Ga,G(u_{0}-u_{j})\rangle
=γj​‖G​a‖2+⟨G​a,G​rj⟩.\displaystyle=\gamma_{j}\left\|Ga\right\|^{2}+\langle Ga,Gr_{j}\rangle. (69)

Since γj>0\gamma_{j}>0, simultaneous success is equivalent to

maxj≤M⟨Ga,G(−rj/γj)⟩<‖Ga‖2.\max_{j\leq M}\langle Ga,G(-r_{j}/\gamma_{j})\rangle<\left\|Ga\right\|^{2}. (70)

Every rjr_{j} is orthogonal to aa. Joint Gaussianity therefore makes G​aGa independent of the family {G(−rj/γj)}j≤M\{G(-r_{j}/\gamma_{j})\}_{j\leq M}. Conditional on Y:=G​aY:=Ga, the process on the left of (70) has the same law as

‖Y‖d{⟨g,−rj/γj⟩}j≤M.\frac{\left\|Y\right\|}{\sqrt{d}}\left\{\langle g,-r_{j}/\gamma_{j}\rangle\right\}_{j\leq M}. (71)

Canceling ‖Y‖>0\left\|Y\right\|>0 and using d​‖Y‖∼χd\sqrt{d}\left\|Y\right\|\sim\chi_{d} proves (68). ∎

Theorem C.1 requires no semantic choice of query and no orthogonality. Correlation changes only the maximum of the fixed Gaussian family. In the isotropic model, that maximum is (1/μ)​maxj≤M​Zj(1/\mu)\max_{j\leq M}Z_{j} up to a common centered Gaussian term, recovering Theorem 4.2. More generally, the critical dimension is the squared typical scale of the Gaussian maximum in (68). The frontier–cumulative comparison remains a comparison under the same bank; the simplified log⁡M/μ2\log M/\mu^{2} form is obtained when the competition geometry is common to both states.

Appendix D Experimental Details and Additional Results

D.1 Dataset and query construction

We use the public graph-4 ProsQA splits released with Zhu et al. (2025b). Table 1 records the full split statistics. The paired width sweep uses every training and test trace and a fixed 120-trace validation subset.

Queries are sampled in coefficient space before the Gaussian embedding. Each query contains the complete terminal frontier but remains strictly partial, uses between 75%75\% and 85.7%85.7\% of the reached history, and has within-support coefficient ratio at most ρ=1.2\rho=1.2. These choices imply the certified cap C=1.386C=1.386; the largest realized caps are smaller on every split. The same query, Gaussian draw, useful candidate, and decoy bank are reused for frontier and cumulative.

D.2 Paired width-sweep configuration

The learned construction is the two-attention router in Theorem 5.3. Its source query and key projections are initialized as I+0.08​Z/dI+0.08Z/\sqrt{d}; the membership inverse temperature and destination temperature are initialized to 88 and 1010 and trained jointly. Frontier and cumulative share all router parameters and optimizer updates. The best epoch is selected by the sum of their validation state cosines.

At test time, success is top-1 retrieval of the fixed useful candidate against 4,096 decoys. Each training seed is evaluated on 419 traces, eight queries per trace, and four Gaussian draws. Statistical intervals are therefore computed across the five independent training seeds, rather than by treating the within-seed evaluations as independent replications. During training, each trace uses one query per epoch, cycling deterministically through the pre-generated eight-query bank; hence four epochs expose four query IDs per trace.

D.3 Complete fixed-query results

Table 4 gives the complete width sweep underlying Figure 3. Intervals are two-sided 95% Student-tt intervals across five training seeds. “Ideal” supplies the analytic state to the same decoder and is not an additional trained model.

The threshold is stable at the individual-seed level (Table 5). The learned cumulative/frontier ratio has mean 0.3910.391 and 95% interval ±0.067\pm 0.067; the fixed-alignment prediction is (μF/μR)2=(0.5011/0.8893)2=0.317(\mu_{F}/\mu_{R})^{2}=(0.5011/0.8893)^{2}=0.317. At d=40d=40, learned-state cosines are 0.966±0.0060.966\pm 0.006 for frontier and 0.933±0.0060.933\pm 0.006 for cumulative. Thus the cumulative accuracy advantage cannot be explained by a higher state cosine.

D.4 Weighted routing protocol and raw codebook results

At d=192d=192, the identity-regularized router is trained for four epochs on 600 traces and six profiles with 64 Gaussian route decoys, AdamW (lr=3×10−3\mathrm{lr}=3\times 10^{-3}, weight decay 10−410^{-4}), clip 1.01.0, accumulation 16, initialization noise 0.020.02, and identity penalty 1010. We select by mean route success minus 0.020.02 projection error on 80 validation traces, 256 Gaussian decoys, and one draw. The frozen checkpoint is evaluated without retraining on five codebooks, 120 test traces, two draws, all unreached graph keys, and 512 additional Gaussian decoys per route step.

The corresponding mean minimum coefficient, normalized by the uniform value, is 1.0001.000, 0.8140.814, and 0.7750.775. The monotone association between this weakest coefficient, joint success, and false positives is the token-level pattern predicted by the amina_{\min} mechanism in Theorem 5.5.

D.5 GPT-2 replication: configuration and complete results

The GPT-2 replication uses the same ProsQA graph-4 traces and the same paired comparison, but replaces the lightweight router with a two-layer causal GPT-2 Transformer. Each edge is represented by causal source and destination tokens followed by one continuous-thought token. The two states share the model, optimizer updates, coefficient-space query, Gaussian codebook, useful candidate, and decoy bank; only the frontier versus cumulative residual update differs. Queries are generated before the Gaussian map, use the full reached support (α=1\alpha=1), and draw positive coefficients with imbalance at most ρ=1.1\rho=1.1.

Each seed–width model is evaluated on 120 held-out traces, four fixed queries per trace, and two Gaussian draws, with the useful candidate ranked against 4,096 fixed decoys. Table 8 reports all tested widths; intervals are two-sided 95% Student-tt intervals over the five model seeds.

The seed-level interpolants in Table 9 are the raw values summarized in the main-text figure. Cumulative has a lower critical dimension for every paired seed; the mean ratio is 0.521±0.0670.521\pm 0.067.

D.6 Weighted routing protocol and raw codebook results

At d=192d=192, the identity-regularized router is trained for four epochs on 600 traces and six profiles with 64 Gaussian route decoys, AdamW (lr=3×10−3\mathrm{lr}=3\times 10^{-3}, weight decay 10−410^{-4}), clip 1.01.0, accumulation 16, initialization noise 0.020.02, and identity penalty 1010. We select by mean route success minus 0.020.02 projection error on 80 validation traces, 256 Gaussian decoys, and one draw. The frozen checkpoint is evaluated without retraining on five codebooks, 120 test traces, two draws, all unreached graph keys, and 512 additional Gaussian decoys per route step.

The corresponding mean minimum coefficient, normalized by the uniform value, is 1.0001.000, 0.8140.814, and 0.7750.775. The monotone association between this weakest coefficient, joint success, and false positives is the token-level pattern predicted by the amina_{\min} mechanism in Theorem 5.5.

D.7 Software and computing resources

We use Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.5.1, CUDA 12.4, NumPy 2.1.3, and Transformers 4.46.2 on NVIDIA A100 GPUs. The lightweight sweep contains 55 trained models and records 37.6 summed GPU-hours; the GPT-2 replication contains 35 single-GPU training runs. The four-width weighted run records 0.17 GPU-hours and its token analysis reuses the d=192d=192 checkpoint.
